title: fix(plugin-timeline): a lookup-typed title or description renders its display name instead of crashing the timeline (objectui#10530)
body:
Fixes #10530

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ObjectTimeline`'s item mapping copied the raw field values onto each item (`title: item[titleField]`, `description: item[descField]`), and `TimelineRenderer` puts both in JSX as React children. The component's own object fetch expands every declared relation through `buildExpandFields(objectDef?.fields)`, so a lookup-typed `titleField` or `descriptionField` arrives as `{ id, name }` and React throws `Objects are not valid as a React child` for the whole rail.

The mapping now derives both slots once, through `@object-ui/core`'s `recordDisplayValueAt`, the same helper `ObjectMap` has read its description through since PR objectui#10525. No new resolver, and `packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts` is not touched.

Files, and nothing else:

- `packages/plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.tsx`: the `recordDisplayValueAt` import and the two mapping lines (plus the comment above them).
- `packages/plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.lookupDisplay-10530.test.tsx`: the new pin, which mirrors `ObjectMap.descriptionDisplay-10456.test.tsx`.
- `.changeset/10530-timeline-lookup-display.md`: `'@object-ui/plugin-timeline': patch`.

## Mechanism hypotheses, measured

Each row was measured with a one-shot probe through the real `ObjectTimeline` and the real `TimelineRenderer`, on base `6ea68e63e` and again on head. The probe was then deleted and never committed.

| # | Hypothesis | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | A lookup-typed title or description crashes the rail | Confirmed on base. The query asked for `$expand` `["account"]`, then the render threw `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {id, name})` for `descriptionField: 'account'` and again for `timeline.titleField: 'account'`. |
| H2 | Mirror the `ObjectMap` precedent | Done: same resolver, same pin structure (reach path, controls, the resolver's empty definition, and a number or boolean arm). |
| H3 | No row that renders today loses its text | Holds for a plain string, a number and a bare id: identical `h3` / `p` text on base and head. **Partly falsified for a boolean:** on base `true` drew an empty title and description element and `false` drew nothing, so neither rendered text today. On head they read `true` / `false`, per the resolver's rule. Other measured moves: a `0` was painted as a bare character beside the line on base and now sits inside it; a whitespace-only value drew an empty-looking line on base and draws none now; a padded string is now trimmed. `null` and `undefined` render nothing on both. |
| H4 | Static `schema.items` go through the same mapping | No. They take the pass-through (`if (schema.items) return schema.items;`), so no mapping runs and no fetch expands anything there. An authored item whose `title` is an object still crashes on head. That path is outside this fix and is listed below. |
| H5 | A lookup-typed `groupByField` reaches JSX as an object | No crash. The group label step stringifies it: both measured rows (accounts Acme and Globex) sat under one header reading `[object Object]`, on base and on head. It is not the same mechanism, so it is not fixed here and is listed below. |
| H6 | The pins | See the next section. |

## Red on base, green on head

The pin file was run on base in a detached compare worktree at `6ea68e63e`, with blob `a46e0f02d` (the same blob as HEAD's), and on the head worktree at `a37ee1039`.

| Arm | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| reach path: the own fetch expands a lookup-typed description (`$expand` contains `account`), and the rail shows `Acme` | FAIL: `the rail must render, not throw: expected 'Objects are not valid as a React chil…' to be null` | pass |
| reach path: the same for `timeline.titleField` | FAIL: same React child error | pass |
| control: a plain string, a number and a bare id in the description | pass | pass |
| control: a plain string, a number and a bare id in the title | pass | pass |
| an expanded record with no display name, a blank value and a padded string | FAIL: `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {id})` | pass |
| a zero or a boolean renders as its string, inside its line | FAIL: `expected [ '' ] to deeply equal [ '0', 'false', 'true' ]` | pass |

Base: `Tests  4 failed | 2 passed (6)`. Head: `Tests  6 passed (6)`.

The server double answers the bare foreign key unless the query asks for `account` in `$expand`. So `Acme` can reach the rail only through the component's own expansion.

## Gates, run at HEAD `a37ee1039`

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-timeline/`: `Test Files  29 passed (29)`, `Tests  338 passed (338)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-timeline run type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. The dependency closure was built first. The new test file is in that program: its first run refused `Array.prototype.at`, which the second commit replaces.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-timeline run lint`: `0 errors`. `ObjectTimeline.tsx` has 26 warnings on base and 26 on head, and the new test file has 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: `2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
- `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`: all exit 0.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: OK.
- `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-shell-escape-residue`, `check-unreferenced-sources`, `check-phantom-dependencies`: all exit 0.
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the three paths: `NOT GOVERNED`.
- Not required, run as insurance: the downstream timeline tests in `plugin-list`, `plugin-view`, `apps/console` and `examples/schema-catalog` (5 files, `Tests  633 passed (633)`).

No doc or README states a lookup title or description behaviour, and no pending changeset does either, so there was nothing to reconcile.

## Acceptance notes

These were found on the way. None of them is filed, and none is fixed here.

- **A lookup-typed `groupByField` groups under `[object Object]`.** This is H5, measured through the real component: records with different accounts merge into one lane, and its header reads `[object Object]`. The site is `ObjectTimeline`'s group-label step, which falls back to `String(m.group)`. Grouping a lookup by display name or by id is a design choice, so this is not a mechanical fix. Not measured at a public door, and no in-repo producer authors a lookup `groupByField` for a timeline. Carrier: none.
- **Static `schema.items` with an object-valued `title` still crash.** This is H4. It is the author-literal pass-through path: no fetch runs and no lookup is expanded there. Carrier: none.
- **Read-only inference, not measured:** `ObjectTimeline`'s `NavigationOverlay` body prints `String(value ?? '—')` for every record key, so an expanded lookup would read `[object Object]` there. `ObjectGallery`'s card title does `String(item[titleField])` for an authored `titleField`, which reads the same way for a lookup. Carrier: none.
